entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.184/2023 dated 24.03.2023 registered at Police Station Gohalpur, District Jabalpur for the offence under Sections 376(2)(n), 294, 323 and 506 of IPC.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
He further submits that prosecutrix is a consenting party.
He also submits that applicant is a student.

entities.text: Teshvendra Patel @ Anmol Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applicant does not have any criminal past.
The applicant is in custody since 13.04.2023 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that applicant is permanent resident of district and there is no likelihood of his absconding from the clutches of law or tamper with prosecution evidence.
He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Hon'ble Court.
Upon these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

T he prosecution case is that on 19.10.2019, the applicant had made sexual relations with the prosecutrix forcibly and later again on the false pretext of marriage, the applicant made sexual relations with the prosecutrix on several occasions.
On 22.03.2023, applicant refused to marry her and also physically assaulted her causing injuries.
MLC report confirms the scratch marks.
Admittedly, prosecutrix was around 20 years of age at the time of first incident that occurred in 2019, and she continued in this relationship for four years.
In the year 2019, the age of the applicant was around 19 years which shows that he was not of marriageable age when he allegedly made a promise to marry.
The long relationship of four years between them appears to be consensual.
In the decision of High Court Nayeem Ahmed Vs. State of M.P., 2023 SCC OnLine SC 89, it has been held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that every breach of promise to marriage is not rape.

entities.text: Nayeem Ahmed Vs. State of M.P., 2023 SCC OnLine SC 89
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case, I find it to be a fit case to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Nitesh Teshvendra Patel @ Anmol Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49547977/
